title: About
text:
I’m a second-year Statistics and Data Science major at the University of California, Los Angeles, minoring in Systems Biology. I graduated from Shorewood High School in 2025 and plan to finish my degree in four years.
I’m interested in the real-world implications of data in fields like environmental science, business practice, sports, and the life sciences. The projects on this site reflect that. I’m hoping to find research or internship experience that combines quantitative work with real questions and actionable solutions.
When I’m not studying, I’m usually triathlon training, watching football, hiking, reading, or playing guitar. I’m also very involved in Christian ministries at UCLA.

title: Projects
text:
Lyon and McAleer Creek Water Quality
R · Quarto · King County & NOAA data
An analysis of 30+ years of King County monitoring data for two urban creeks feeding Lake Washington, covering summer temperature, dissolved oxygen, and storm-driven copper. Summer temperatures step upward after 2013, dissolved oxygen declines on a separate and longer timeline, and storm copper rises with rainfall once samples are joined to NOAA precipitation records. Built for the Lake Forest Park Stewardship Foundation’s Streamkeepers, with a public log of analysis decisions.
Read the report → View on GitHub →


Urban Coyotes in California
R · sf · Quarto
An exploratory analysis of ~24,000 GBIF wildlife observation records, examining urban vs. non-urban coyote sightings across geography, time, and season (with attention to the limits of citizen-science data).
Read the report → View on GitHub →


Breast Cancer Subtyping from Gene Expression in progress
An analysis of ~1,200 TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq samples reproducing the established four-subtype molecular classification, then extended to test whether long non-coding RNAs recover the same structure as protein-coding genes.
